input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: The first Section 7.2 imposes an MFN-style obligation on us: before engaging another provider we must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer we receive. That is open-ended — no defined product, no time limit, and no like-for-like comparison carve-outs — so it fails the fallback and approaches walk-away territory, and it contradicts Section 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment. This is a disclose-and-match mechanic only and is not double-flagged as exclusivity. The redline replaces the obligation with an express confirmation that no disclose-or-match obligation applies, achieving the preferred position; Vendor-granted MFN pricing in our favour remains welcome.

proposal.summary: Replace the Customer-side disclose-and-match MFN obligation with an express statement that no such obligation applies.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have removed the requirement that we disclose and match any more favourable third-party offer for Vendor and confirmed that no such obligation applies, since our playbook does not accept an MFN running against us and this clause contradicted Section 12.3's acknowledgement that we made no most-favoured-customer commitment.

ops.oldText: Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
ops.newText: Customer has no obligation to disclose or match for Vendor any commercial offer it receives.

mappings.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
